originalTitle: Traders now see little chance of a Fed rate hike in October after weak jobs report
summary: Odds tumbled after a jobs report showed a soft labor market, leading more traders to lower the the chances of a fed funds rate increase this month.
content:
Investors now think the odds are extremely unlikely that the Federal Reserve raises interest rates again in October, following a weaker-than-expected September employment report .

CME's FedWatch tool, based on trading in 30-day interest rate futures, shows only a 17% chance that the Fed increases rates by a quarter percentage point. One week ago, odds were close to 36%. On prediction market platform Kalshi, chances for a hike in October stood at just 18%, down from almost 70% a week ago.

The U.S. economy added only 29,000 jobs in September, below estimates for a gain of more than 80,000. A softer labor market could recalibrate the Fed's thinking in how it balances its dual mandate to ensure full employment and steady prices, after it raised interest rates at its September meeting to combat inflation that's remained above target for five years .

Odds for a hike in October also fell in the middle of this week after the release of the personal consumption expenditures price index , the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, on Wednesday showed cooler-than-expected prices. Core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 3% in August, lighter than consensus estimates for a rise of 3.3%.

"This report strengthens the case for the Federal Reserve to remain patient," said Adam Schickling, a senior economist at Vanguard. "The labor market has not deteriorated sharply, but there is also little evidence that it has meaningfully strengthened, giving policymakers reason to wait for additional data."

While traders now think a hike in October is unlikely, they're still forecasting that the central bank will raise rates in December.

On FedWatch, odds are above 75% for a hike in December, while on Kalshi there are 65% odds that the Fed raises rates.

The Federal Reserve is set to announce its next decision on interest rates at the conclusion of a two-day policy meeting on Oct. 28.

— CNBC's Michelle Fox contributed reporting

Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.
chineseTitle: 由于就业报告疲弱，交易员现在认为美联储十月份加息的可能性很小
chineseSummary: 就业报告显示劳动力市场疲软后，赔率大幅下跌，导致更多交易员降低本月联邦基金利率加息的可能性。
chineseContent:
投资者现在认为，在 9 月份就业报告弱于预期之后，美联储 10 月份再次加息的可能性极小。

CME 的 FedWatch 工具基于 30 天利率期货交易，显示美联储加息 0.25 个百分点的可能性只有 17%。一周前，这一可能性接近 36%。在预测市场平台 Kalshi 上，10 月份加息的可能性仅为 18%，低于一周前的近 70%。

9 月份美国经济仅增加了 29,000 个就业岗位，低于预期的 80,000 多个就业岗位。劳动力市场走软可能会重新调整美联储在如何平衡其双重使命以确保充分就业和物价稳定方面的思路，此前美联储在9月份的会议上加息以应对五年来一直高于目标的通胀。

在周三公布的个人消费支出价格指数（美联储首选的通胀指标）显示价格低于预期后，十月份加息的可能性也在本周中下降。 8 月份，不包括食品和能源的核心价格上涨 3%，低于市场普遍预期的 3.3% 涨幅。

先锋集团高级经济学家亚当·希克林表示：“这份报告强化了美联储保持耐心的理由。” “劳动力市场并未急剧恶化，但也没有什么证据表明劳动力市场明显走强，这让政策制定者有理由等待更多数据。”

尽管交易员现在认为 10 月份加息的可能性不大，但他们仍然预测央行将在 12 月份加息。

FedWatch 认为 12 月加息的可能性高于 75%，而 Kalshi 认为美联储加息的可能性为 65%。

美联储将于 10 月 28 日为期两天的政策会议结束时宣布下一次利率决定。

— CNBC 的米歇尔·福克斯 (Michelle Fox) 贡献报道

披露：CNBC 和 Kalshi 之间存在商业关系，包括客户获取和少数股权投资。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
